coverage: Curated operational AI-governance regimes with concrete provider, deployer, employer, platform, or practitioner evidence duties; not a 50-state survey. It excludes most biometric-only, deepfake, election, intellectual-property, publicity-right, takedown, and procurement-only laws.

jurisdictions.applicability: Publicly available generative AI systems or services within the statutory scope.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Training-data source, type, ownership, licensing, personal-data and modification disclosures are not authorization events.

jurisdictions.applicability: Qualifying frontier developers meeting statutory thresholds.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Frontier thresholds, safety evaluations, framework disclosures and critical-incident facts remain external.

jurisdictions.date_verification_note: Enactment is verified by the official signing announcement. January 1 is the ordinary effective date; an applicable special operative clause could not be checked because enrolled-text retrieval was blocked.
jurisdictions.applicability: Organizations seeking state certification to independently assess AI systems and models for safety, risk, or conformity with applicable state-law criteria.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Certification, independence, assessment design, model access, safety tests and findings are external; authorization-event metrics are not an independent verification.

jurisdictions.date_verification_note: Enactment is verified by the official signing announcement. January 1 is the ordinary effective date; an applicable special operative clause could not be checked because enrolled-text retrieval was blocked.
jurisdictions.applicability: AI auditors within the enacted state registry and its independence, transparency and integrity standards.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Auditor registration, conflicts, qualifications, audit scope, methods and conclusions are external artifacts; apparitor does not certify an auditor or an AI system.

jurisdictions.measure: SB 942, as amended by AB 853 and AB 2713
jurisdictions.date_verification_note: Official author notices disagree on the first implementation day. Consolidated statutory text was unavailable during verification; neither day is asserted as verified. AB 2713's later amendment has an inferred ordinary 2027-01-01 effective date; special operative clauses remain unverified.
jurisdictions.applicability: Generative-AI providers and specified platforms or capture-device manufacturers within the California AI Transparency Act's role-specific scope, including the 2026 system-provenance amendment.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Detection tools, manifest and latent disclosures, platform provenance handling, and generated-content facts are external artifacts; authorization events do not establish them.

jurisdictions.applicability: Operators making a companion chatbot platform available to California users within the statutory definitions and exceptions.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Disclosure presentation, user-age handling, break reminders, self-harm protocols, and statutory platform reports remain external; do not place conversation or health content in authorization logs.

jurisdictions.applicability: Covered ADMT materially influencing consequential decisions in enumerated domains.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Decision inputs, explanations, discrimination analysis, consumer requests and reconsideration remain external.

jurisdictions.applicability: Employer AI use in recruitment and enumerated employment decisions.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Employment notices and protected-class discrimination analysis require external governed records.

jurisdictions.applicability: Developers within the amended frontier-model statutory thresholds.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Model safety evaluation and statutory incident evidence remain external.

jurisdictions.applicability: Role- and use-specific disclosures and prohibited AI uses under the enacted Act.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Consumer disclosures, purpose evidence, biometric facts and discrimination analysis remain external.

jurisdictions.applicability: Licensed or otherwise authorized practitioners using AI for diagnosis or treatment recommendations, and covered entities subject to the electronic-health-record chapter.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Practitioner review, patient disclosure, medical-record standards, and EHR safeguards require governed clinical records; authorization logs must not contain protected health information.

jurisdictions.applicability: Use of generative AI in covered consumer transactions and regulated services.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Required disclosure delivery and regulated-service records remain external.

jurisdictions.applicability: Suppliers of AI systems that engage in conversations similar to confidential communications with a mental-health therapist and are made available to Utah users within statutory scope.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Disclosure delivery, chatbot policies, development and monitoring evidence, and personal-information controls remain external; never log user input or health content here.

jurisdictions.applicability: Proposed framework for high-risk AI in consequential decisions.
jurisdictions.external_gap: All proposed audit conclusions require external evaluation artifacts.

jurisdictions.applicability: Proposed civil-rights framework for covered algorithms in consequential decisions.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Protected-class and performance analyses require separate governed evaluation data.

jurisdictions.applicability: Use of an AEDT to screen NYC candidates or employees within the rule's scope.
jurisdictions.external_gap: Selection rates, impact ratios, independent-auditor evidence and notices are external.
